purpose: Sanity-check the silver-calibrated automation threshold (evidence_score>=0.30, intent_confidence>=0.80), chosen via scripts/evaluate_automation.py on the SILVER test set, against the untouched human-verified golden set. This threshold was NOT re-tuned on the golden set (that would be exactly the golden-set overfitting the assignment warns against) -- it is simply evaluated as-is.
conclusion: The silver-based 99% auto-precision claim does not hold up against human-verified labels. Even the upper bound of the 95% CI on the golden-set measurement (82.1%) is well below 99%. This is the central finding for reports/misleading_headline_number.md: the silver-label pipeline (cluster-derived training labels evaluated on cluster-derived test labels) substantially overstates real-world intent accuracy and, downstream, auto-handling precision. The golden-set measurement (68.75%, 95% CI 51.4-82.1%) is the trustworthy number, at n=32 auto-handled cases -- a real limitation of only having 200 hand-labeled examples to spend on this check. A production deployment would need a substantially larger hand-labeled sample before trusting a specific precision number at this operating point.
recommendation: Report both numbers, prominently and side by side, with this gap as the headline honesty finding, not a footnote. Do not present 99% as the project's headline auto-precision claim without this caveat immediately adjacent to it.
